Your first five minutes

  1. Open Copilot Chat. Go to m365.cloud.microsoft/chat, or select Copilot in Teams or Outlook.
  2. Try one prompt. Pick anything from the Prompt Library, fill in the [brackets] and send it.
  3. Summarize a long email thread. In Outlook, open a long conversation and select Summary by Copilot.
  4. Turn on your Daily Digest. See Agents & Tools.
  5. Watch a two-minute video. Start with Demo Videos.

Where Copilot lives

AppTry this first
Copilot ChatAttach a document and ask for a summary with deadlines and dollar amounts.
OutlookSummarize a thread, draft a reply, or get coaching on a sensitive email.
WordCheck defined terms and cross-references, or explain a provision in plain English.
ExcelAsk questions of a rent roll or deal list (format it as a table first).
TeamsGet a recap of a transcribed meeting with action items and owners.

How to write a good prompt

Give Copilot four things:

  • Goal: what you want ("an open-issues list").
  • Context: the matter, the audience, why you need it.
  • Source: the emails or files to use. Type / to pick them.
  • Expectations: format, length, and what to do when it isn't sure ("write not found rather than guessing").

Not sure how to ask? Tell Copilot what you want and ask it to write the prompt for you.

Agents are Copilot helpers built for one job at Cassin. Each one works with your own sign-in and only sees what you can already see. The AI Working Group picks what we build next, so if there's a workflow you'd like help with, suggest it.

Five habits

  1. Use the firm's Copilot for client work. Microsoft 365 Copilot runs inside the firm's Microsoft 365 environment and only sees what you can already see. Don't paste client or matter information into public AI tools such as free ChatGPT or Gemini.
  2. Check before you rely. Click the citations. Compare figures, dates, names and section numbers against the source. Copilot can be confidently wrong.
  3. A lawyer reviews it before it leaves the firm. Anything going to a client, a lender or the other side gets attorney review, the same as work from a junior colleague.
  4. Ask it to say when it doesn't know. Add "write not found rather than guessing" to prompts that pull facts from documents.
  5. Keep the firm's rules. Follow the firm's policies for client and confidential information, records and ethical walls. AI doesn't change them.

What Copilot can see

Only email, chats, meetings and files that you already have permission to open. It doesn't give you access to anything new.

Where your prompts go

Microsoft doesn't use your prompts, responses or files to train its AI models.

Not sure?

Ask the AI Working Group before you try it on a live matter.
